title: Panthay Rebellion
capsule: The Panthay Rebellion was a Muslim Hui uprising in Yunnan province against Qing rule, ignited in 1856 by ethnic violence in the mining districts and growing resentment of Han settler privilege. Du Wenxiu (Sultan Suleiman) established a sultanate at Dali and governed much of western Yunnan for nearly two decades, maintaining diplomatic contact with Britain through Burma and briefly threatening Qing authority over the whole province. Qing forces under岑毓英 (Cen Yuying) mounted a sustained reconquest campaign and retook Dali in January 1873; Du Wenxiu surrendered and was executed, ending the sultanate after an estimated 800,000 to several million deaths from violence and famine across Yunnan.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The core area of the sultanate around Dali and western Yunnan is documented, but the fluid frontier between rebel-controlled and Qing-controlled zones within the province shifted constantly and is not precisely mapped.
